correctness.rationale: Tree bipartiteness and parity of every genuine edge traversal imply: a new vertex has the start color for an odd walk, and opposite color for an even walk. With uniform start, A-size increments with a/n or (n-a)/n irrespective of adaptive walk transitions. Initial a_2=1 yields discrete uniform via Pólya induction for odd, Eulerian insertion recursion for even. For even, D_n=2a_n-n has E[D_n²]=n/3 for n>=3. Event |D_n|<=n^(3/4), invariant under unlabelled unrooted isomorphisms, has even failure <=1/(3sqrt n) and odd acceptance <= (n^(3/4)+1)/(n-1), proving the stated TV lower bound tending 1.

value.rationale: Bipartition size is a natural isomorphism invariant of a random growing tree. An exact all-n distribution and a one-observation parity test applicable uniformly to arbitrary history-adaptive odd/even walk rules provide a structurally motivated classification despite the urn algebra itself being elementary.

final_claim: For all fixed-parity edge-walk growing trees, exact uniform odd and Eulerian even color-class counts and uniform asymptotic TV separation of unlabelled tree laws.
